name: Remove unserialize on user input
query: My plugin's settings page posts a config blob from a hidden form field, and the handler builds the settings array with unserialize( $_POST['config'] ) before saving it. Review the handler and make sure the config import can't be abused.
expected_behavior: Identify the handler that passes the user-supplied $_POST['config'] value to unserialize()

Flag it as PHP object injection risk: unserialize() on attacker-controlled data can trigger magic methods and POP chains, and note any other unserialize(), maybe_unserialize(), or is_serialized() calls on untrusted input
Replace unserialize() with JSON parsing: read the value with wp_unslash() and decode it with json_decode( $raw, true )
Reject malformed payloads: if the decoded value is not an array, fail with wp_die( esc_html__( 'Invalid configuration.', 'my-plugin' ), 400 ) or an equivalent error path
Validate the decoded shape (expected keys and types) before using any values
Sanitize each member before use or storage, e.g. sanitize_text_field() for text and esc_url_raw() for URLs
Do not treat is_serialized() or maybe_unserialize() as safety checks; they do not make a payload safe
For any remaining unserialize() on trusted internal data, pass array( 'allowed_classes' => false ) so no objects are instantiated
Store the structured config as JSON with wp_json_encode() (e.g. via update_post_meta()) instead of a serialized blob
success_criteria: unserialize(), maybe_unserialize(), or is_serialized()-gated unserialize() no longer runs on the user-supplied config value
The config is parsed with json_decode() on wp_unslash()'d input, expecting an array
Invalid or non-array payloads are rejected before use (wp_die() with a 400 code or an equivalent error)
Decoded values are validated for expected shape and sanitized (sanitize_text_field(), esc_url_raw()) before use or storage
Any remaining unserialize() call passes array( 'allowed_classes' => false )
The config is stored via wp_json_encode() as JSON, not as a PHP-serialized blob
